title: How to Compress Audio for WhatsApp on iPhone
description: Need a smaller audio file to send in WhatsApp? Export a lower-bitrate MP3 or M4A copy, listen to it, then share that copy. If size is not a problem, try sending the original as a document first.
direct: Need a smaller audio file to send in WhatsApp? Export a lower-bitrate MP3 or M4A copy, listen to it, then share that copy. If size is not a problem, try sending the original as a document first.

cards.document.heading: Only need to attach the file?
cards.document.body: In WhatsApp, tap +, choose Document, then select the saved audio in Files. The official iPhone help lists a 2 GB document limit. This sends a file attachment, not a newly recorded voice message.
cards.smaller.heading: Need a smaller transfer?
cards.smaller.body: Compression is useful on a slow connection or when the recipient needs a smaller copy. Keep the original, especially for music or audio you plan to edit.
sections.quality.heading: Compare bytes and sound, not loudness
sections.quality.body: File compression reduces storage size. It does not make a quiet recording louder. Converting an already compact file can produce little saving or even a larger copy; check the export rather than relying on its extension.
sections.failure.heading: Still cannot send it?
sections.failure.body: Try a small known-good file. If that also fails, check the connection, available storage and WhatsApp permissions. A compressor cannot repair those problems. We do not apply a universal 16 MB rule to every WhatsApp attachment route.

steps.import.text: Open the saved recording in Audio Compressor MP3 Converter and choose Compress. Use MP3 or M4A for a smaller listening copy.
steps.quality.text: Start with Medium. For speech, try Small only if you still need fewer bytes. Preview quiet words and background sounds before accepting the quality loss.
steps.send.text: Export, check the actual saved file size, and share the copy to WhatsApp. Alternatively, save it to Files and attach it through + → Document.
